title: Can Acceleration in Gradient-Norm Minimization Be Anytime? Sharp Last-Iterate Limits in Smooth Convex Optimization
summary: In smooth convex optimization, the gradient norm is a directly observable measure of stationarity. Accelerating a first-order method that minimizes the gradient norm is known to be more delicate than accelerating the minimization of function values. Optimal accelerated methods such as OGM-G (Kim & Fessler, 2021) are known to exist for any prescribed finite horizon, but their coefficients depend explicitly on the length of that horizon, i.e. the number of iterations.
